account.desc: The username and password this server is reached with. Changing either signs out every other session, which is the point: the reason to rotate a credential is that the old one may be known.

agents.idHint: Used in links, in the config file, and as the name the model sees when another agent delegates to this one.
agents.idPreview: Will be renamed to “{{id}}”. Delegations and conversations follow; bookmarks and other devices do not.
agents.idTaken: There is already an agent called “{{id}}”.
agents.limitsDesc: The budget a turn runs inside.
agents.missingNotice: “{{id}}” is no longer configured. This conversation runs on the default agent until you choose another.
agents.newHint: It starts as a copy of the default agent — its model, budget, prompt and permissions — and is its own from there.
agents.note: Each holds its own prompt, model, permissions and memory. A new one is created as a copy of the default agent’s.
agents.promptDesc: Everything this agent is told before a conversation starts. It is yours to rewrite — the workspace jail and the tool approvals are enforced in code and do not read a word of it.
agents.subagentPromptHint: The tool description the model reads, so it is what decides when the subagent is used. Left empty it uses the sentence shown, which names the agent and follows a rename.
agents.subagentsDesc: Agents this one can hand a task to. Each becomes a tool it can call; the subagent works in its own context and returns a written answer.
agents.subagentsEmpty: No subagents. This agent does all its own work.
agents.subagentsNoneAvailable: There is no other agent to delegate to yet. Create one, and it can be added here.
agents.title: Agents
agents.toolboxAllowHint: CIDR blocks, comma separated — 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.1.0/24. Host names are refused because DNS rebinding defeats them.
agents.toolboxDesc: Which box of tools this agent works in. A toolbox is a container image plus its whole security policy, installed and approved by you — this screen can point at one and narrow its network, never widen it.
agents.toolboxHost: None — run commands on this machine
agents.toolboxNoProfiles: No toolboxes installed. Build one with toolboxes/build.sh, then approve it.
agents.toolboxNotApproved: Not approved yet — approve it with `ghost toolbox approve` before an agent can use it.
agents.toolsDesc: Which tools this agent may call, and what happens when it does. A tool set to Disabled is not offered to the model at all.

chat.approvalClosed: The approval window closed. The call was refused.
chat.externalImage: External image — opens in a new tab rather than loading here

noAnswer.reasoningOnly: The model finished its reasoning without writing an answer. Nothing was lost — regenerating usually produces one.
noAnswer.silent: The model returned nothing at all: no answer, and no tool call. Regenerating usually produces one.

chat.offline: Offline — messages will be sent when the connection returns.

stopReasons.error: The turn ended with an error.
stopReasons.max_iterations: Stopped after reaching the iteration limit for one turn.
stopReasons.wall_timeout: Stopped after reaching the time limit for one turn.

chat.turnRunning: A turn is running. Enter queues your message.
chat.welcomeHint: Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line · @ to scope the turn
chat.welcomeNote: The agent reads and writes inside its workspace, and asks before it runs a command or reaches the network. Every tool call shows up in the transcript with its arguments and its output.

common.name: Name
common.notFoundBody: There is nothing at this address.

context.intro: What a turn on this conversation would send to the model right now.
context.nothingYet: Nothing to measure yet — this conversation has not started. Send a message and the budget appears here.
context.title: Context

files.conflict: This file changed on disk since it was opened — most likely the agent wrote to it. Your edits are still here. Reload to take the version on disk and lose them, or copy what you need out first.
files.emptyHint: Drop files anywhere in this box to upload them, or use the Upload button.
files.folderContents_one: Everything inside goes with it — {{count}} item.
files.folderContents_other: Everything inside goes with it — {{count}} items.
files.notText: This file is not text, so there is nothing to show or edit here. Download it to open it in something that understands it.
files.title: Files
files.tooBig: This file is {{size}} and only the first part was read. Saving would delete the rest, so it cannot be edited here — download it instead.

notifications.empty: Automation runs and expired approvals report themselves here.
notifications.title: Notifications

providers.connectionDesc: Where to reach it, and what to open it with. Keys go to the encrypted vault and are never returned by the API.
providers.deleteHint: {{name}} is removed from the settings, and its saved key is deleted with it. Re-adding an endpoint with the same name does not bring the key back.
providers.identityDesc: What this endpoint is called in the list.
providers.newHint: One endpoint. The type is fixed once it exists — add the same type twice to run against two servers, and they keep separate keys.
providers.none: No providers yet. Add one, then choose a model on the agent that will use it.
providers.panelDesc: Each row is one endpoint. Add the same type more than once to run against two servers — they keep separate keys, and a key is written to the encrypted vault and never returned by the API.
providers.reachableNoModels: Reachable, though it listed no models.
providers.title: Providers

appearance.languageDesc: What this install speaks. It applies to the web UI and to `ghost chat` on this server, not only to this browser.
appearance.languageHint: `System` follows your browser until someone chooses otherwise.
appearance.themeDesc: Whether the interface is light or dark. This one is yours alone — it is stored in this browser and never written to the config.

settings.loadError: The settings file could not be read and defaults are in use. Saving here overwrites it. ({{error}})

tools.approvalDesc: How long a prompt stays open. Which tools ask at all is set per agent, on the agent’s own screen.
tools.approvalTimeoutHint: An unanswered prompt is denied after this. Unlike the other durations here, 0 is not allowed — an approval that never expires holds the turn open forever.
tools.enableExecHint: The install-wide switch. Off removes exec from every agent, whatever its own permission says. On means each agent decides for itself, on its own screen.
tools.executionDesc: The exec tool, and what it may produce.
tools.maxCharsHint: Longer results are truncated head and tail, keeping both ends. There is no unlimited: this number also bounds how much of a file a single read loads, so set it high rather than to 0.
tools.restrictFiles: Restrict file tools to the workspace
tools.resultsDesc: What comes back from a tool, and from where.

setup.asking: Asking the provider what it has…
setup.codeNote: It was printed in the terminal that started this server. It works once.
setup.languageNote: The rest of this wizard, and the app afterwards, will be in it. You can change it later in Settings.
setup.modelNote: Listed by the provider itself where it can be asked. Anything else can be typed in.
setup.passwordNote: This agent can read and write files and run commands. Pick something you would use for a login.
setup.providerNote: A local server like Ollama, or a cloud provider. You can add more later, including a second one of the same type.

tool.subagentUnavailable: The subagent’s steps are no longer stored.
tool.truncated: Output was truncated in the middle to fit the tool-output budget. The model saw the same thing.

turn.none: No figures were recorded for this turn.

workspaces.blocked_one: {{count}} conversation still belongs to {{workspace}}. Moving them to Default keeps their history; the files stay where they are either way.
workspaces.blocked_other: {{count}} conversations still belong to {{workspace}}. Moving them to Default keeps their history; the files stay where they are either way.
workspaces.defaultNote: The folder that holds every other workspace, so a turn in it can reach their files. It cannot be detached.
workspaces.deleteHint: {{workspace}} is detached from GhostAI. Its folder and everything in it stays on disk, and recreating a workspace on the same folder adopts it again.
workspaces.filter: Filter workspaces by name or folder
workspaces.folderDefault: The default workspace is the root every other one is a directory inside, so it has no folder of its own to move.
workspaces.folderHint: The directory created under the workspace root. Leave it blank to use the one derived from the name.
workspaces.folderHintEdit: The directory this workspace’s files are in, under the workspace root. Changing it moves the folder and brings its conversations with it; links already shared for its files stop resolving.
workspaces.folderReserved: That folder name is reserved and cannot name a workspace.
workspaces.folderShape: Use 1–40 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.
workspaces.folderTaken: A workspace already uses that folder.
workspaces.identityDesc: What this workspace is called, and where its files are.
workspaces.namedNote_one: Isolated from the other named workspaces — it cannot reach their files, and they cannot reach its. {{count}} conversation runs in it, last updated {{updated}}.
workspaces.namedNote_other: Isolated from the other named workspaces — it cannot reach their files, and they cannot reach its. {{count}} conversations run in it, last updated {{updated}}.
workspaces.newHint: A name, and the folder it gets inside the workspace root. Neither is a path, and the two are independent — the folder only starts out derived from the name.
workspaces.note: A workspace is a folder the agent works in. Default holds all the others, so it can reach their files; the named ones cannot reach each other.
workspaces.title: Workspaces
